title: Corrected Claims after a Billing-Correction Reversal — Prescription Insurance on File Desk Guidance
content:
## When a corrected claim is owed

Under **Prescription Insurance on File**, a claim the plan paid and that was then reversed to correct a billing mistake is owed a corrected claim. The corrected claim is re-billed on the retroactive re-bill basis (`retro_rebill`) on the original date of service, for the fill the reversed claim paid for, and the corrected claim names the reversed claim: on the plan's claim ledger it stands as a re-billed claim naming the reversed claim it replaces.

## Recording the corrected claim: `rebill_corrected_claim_b015fa67`

**Capability.** One call records one paid claim on the patient's insurance plan on file on the re-bill basis (`retro_rebill`), with no override code, the original date of service, and the fill number, days supply, quantity and patient pay given, together with the reference number of the reversed claim it replaces. Nothing else changes. Afterwards the plan's claim history shows the corrected claim naming the claim it replaces, with its patient pay.

**Invocation.** An agent-side tool: the desk unlocks `rebill_corrected_claim_b015fa67` and calls it.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `customer_id` | The patient reference number, as returned by the patient profile lookup | Id |
| `coverage_id` | The reference number of the insurance plan on file the corrected claim is billed to, as returned by the insurance plan lookup | Id |
| `prescription_id` | The reference number of the prescription the corrected claim is for, as shown on the reversed claim returned by the claim history lookup | Id |
| `claim_id` | The reference number of the earlier paid claim that was reversed for the billing correction and that this corrected claim replaces, as returned by the claim history lookup; it is recorded on the corrected claim | Id |
| `fill_id` | The reference number of the dispensing entry the corrected claim pays for, as returned by the dispensing history lookup | Id |
| `fill_number` | The fill number of that dispensing entry, exactly as shown on it | Integer: 0 for an original fill, 1 upward for refills |
| `service_date` | The original date of service of that dispensing entry, exactly as shown on it | YYYY-MM-DD |
| `days_supply_billed` | The days supply the corrected claim bills — the days supply the dispensing entry actually supplied | Integer days |
| `quantity_billed` | The quantity the corrected claim bills — the quantity the dispensing entry actually dispensed | Integer dosage units |
| `patient_pay_usd` | The patient pay of the corrected claim | USD, a positive amount with 2 decimal places, rounded to the cent |

**Return.** On success, a dictionary printed as text with `status` (`claim_paid`), `claim_id` (the reference number of the new corrected claim), `source_claim_id` (the reversed claim it replaces), `claim_basis` (always `retro_rebill`), `event_date` (the date of service, YYYY-MM-DD) and `patient_pay_usd` (USD, 2 decimal places).

*Illustration of a return (hypothetical values):* a call with a `service_date` of 2025-04-02 and a `patient_pay_usd` of 18.75 returns an `event_date` of 2025-04-02 — the original date of service, not the day of the call — and a `patient_pay_usd` of 18.75, with `source_claim_id` equal to the `claim_id` passed.
